title: Scientific Monitoring of the Introduction of Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Immunisation in Germany: Acceptance, Implementation and Effectiveness – Qualitative Study in Module 1
summary: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections are a common cause of serious respiratory illness in infants. Since 2024, RSV immunisation has been available in Germany, which protects infants from RSV and is recommended for all newborns and infants by the German vaccination commission. Depending on the timing of birth, this intervention can be administered in paediatric practices or maternity hospitals; antenatal care plays a role in informing expectant parents. Healthcare professionals play a key role in ensuring that as many infants as possible receive this protection: through high-quality counselling and a clear recommendation. This study examines the factors that facilitate or hinder healthcare professionals in recommending and administering RSV immunisation in practice. To this end, interviews with healthcare professionals from various care settings will be conducted and analysed.
conditions: Implementation of RSV immunisation by healthcare professionals

interventions.name: We will conduct individual qualitative expert interviews with healthcare professionals in Germany.
